summary:
Li–Liu study the Chow group of the motive of a tempered global L-packet π of U(r, r) over a CM extension E/F with F ≠ Q, V^ram_F = ∅ and every 2-adic place split, when the global root number is −1. The main results:
- Theorem 1.5: if L′(1/2, π) ≠ 0 and Hypothesis 6.6 (Galois action on the π-part of middle cohomology) holds, the π-nearly isotypic localization of the Chow group of the unitary Shimura variety X_L is nonzero.
- Theorem 1.7: assuming in addition the modularity of Kudla's generating functions (Hypothesis 4.5), the Beilinson–Bloch height of arithmetic theta lifts equals L′(1/2, π)/b_{2r}(0) times C_r^{[F:Q]} times normalized local doubling zeta integrals. This is Liu's arithmetic inner product formula.
- Corollary 1.9: an explicit formula for new vectors.

The proof chooses Hecke operators that temper the cycles (Appendix B). Beilinson's height of the special cycles then decomposes into local indices, which are identified with the Fourier coefficients of E′(0, g, Φ):
- at split places, by vanishing on Drinfeld-level models (§7, using Caraiani–Scholze);
- at inert places, through the Li–Zhang local identities on smooth and semistable RSZ models (§§8–9);
- at archimedean places, after averaging against a cusp form (§10).
The doubling method with regular test functions (Proposition 3.13, Appendix A) supplies the analytic side (§3).

The libraries have none of this. The atlas plans the standard inputs: Fourier theory AL.0, the Weil representation MP.2–MP.3, the doubling method AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4, Arthur's multiplicity formula ML.4, Galois representations AG2.2/AG2.5, Shimura varieties V1/V6, cycle classes EDC.3, Hochschild–Serre R02.2, weights R34.5, the weight spectral sequence LPV.7, K-theory with supports S.6–S.7, Chern classes M.8, and Igusa varieties IG.1/IG.4/IG.5.

Routes:
- the arithmetic inner product formula, including Beilinson's local indices, to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22;
- the integral models to UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels, and the integral special cycles and Li–Zhang identities to UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles, both candidates of PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B;
- sources: local theta results to MP.3, Lemma 7.3 to IG.5/IG.7, absolute purity to SF.2, and the Beilinson–Bloch conjecture to MC.7.

Nine source issues are recorded.
- E1 and E2, and the citation gap E9, are corrected in the authors' final version but remain in arXiv v5: the constant C_r (2^{r(r−1)} for 2^{−2r}), and a choice of current in the archimedean proof.
- E3 is new. Proposition 9.1 uses Li–Zhang Theorem 10.5.1, which Li–Zhang state is conditional on their Conjecture 10.4.1. The main theorems therefore carried an unstated hypothesis until Li–Rapoport–Zhang (arXiv:2404.02214, Theorem 14.6.2).
- E4–E8 are misprints.
- E10 and E11 are the authors' own errata, published in Disegni–Liu (2024) §4.10: the identification of χ^R_{π^∨} with (χ^R_π)^c (harmless), and two false formulae in the proof of Lemma 4.4, whose statement is reproved there after Shah's arXiv:2310.01677.

items.name: The equivariant Beilinson–Bloch conjecture (1.1) and Beilinson's positivity conjecture (conjectures)
items.statement: For X projective smooth over a number field E of odd dimension 2r − 1 with an algebra T acting by étale correspondences, and ϱ an irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation of T: dim_C Hom_T(ϱ, CH^r(X)^0_C) = ord_{s=0} L(s, Hom_T(ϱ, H^{2r−1}(X ⊗_E Ē, Q_ℓ(r))_C)) (1.1), refining rank CH^r(X)^0 = ord_{s=0} L(s, H^{2r−1}(X_Ē, Q_ℓ(r))) [Beĭ87, Conj. 5.9; Blo84]. Beilinson's positivity conjecture [Beĭ87, Conj. 5.5]: (−1)^r⟨c, c⟩ ≥ 0 for primitive homologically trivial cycles c of codimension r (used in Remark 1.10 together with injectivity of the étale Abel–Jacobi map).
items.locator: Introduction, (1.1), pp.2–3; Remark 1.10, p.8, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Conjectures, stated only. Routed to MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.7 as a source.

items.name: Conjecture 1.1 (Beilinson–Bloch for unitary Shimura varieties), conjecture
items.statement: Let π be a tempered cuspidal automorphic representation of G_r(A_F), G_r = U(W_r) quasi-split of rank n = 2r, and V a hermitian space over E of rank n of signature (n − 1, 1) at the real place induced by ι and (n, 0) at the others, H = U(V). For every irreducible admissible representation π̃^∞ of H(A^∞_F) with π̃^∞_v ≃ π_v for almost all v where H_v ≃ G_{r,v}, and Hom_{H(A^∞_F)}(π̃^∞, colim_L H^{n−1}_dR(X_L/C)) ≠ 0: dim_C Hom_{H(A^∞_F)}(π̃^∞, colim_L CH^r(X_L)^0_C) = ord_{s=1/2} L(s, Π_{j(π̃^∞)}), where Π_{j(π̃^∞)} is the cuspidal factor of BC(π) determined by π̃^∞ (Lemma 3.15). Remark 1.2: it should be formulable with totally positive definite incoherent hermitian spaces and incoherent Shimura varieties without fixing ι.
items.locator: Conjecture 1.1 and Remark 1.2, pp.3–4, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: A conjecture, stated only. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Assumption 1.3, Remark 1.4, and the invariants R_π, S_π, ε(π), V_π
items.statement: Assumption 1.3: V^ram_F = ∅ and V^spl_F contains all 2-adic places (so [F:Q] is even); π cuspidal on G_r(A_F) with π_v holomorphic discrete series of Harish-Chandra parameter {(1−n)/2, …, (n−1)/2} at archimedean v, a principal series at split v, unramified or almost unramified (in the sense of [Liu22, Def. 5.3]) with respect to K_{r,v} at inert v (v unramified over Q if almost unramified), and tempered at finite v. R_π ⊆ V^spl_F: π_v ramified; S_π ⊆ V^int_F: π_v almost unramified. Then ε(π) = (−1)^{r[F:Q]+|S_π|}; π determines by local theta dichotomy a totally positive definite hermitian space V_π over A_E with ϵ(V_{π,v}) = 1 iff v ∉ S_π; |S_π| odd iff ε(π) = −1 iff V_π is incoherent.
items.locator: Assumption 1.3 and Remark 1.4, pp.4–5, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Remark 1.4(2): condition (2) is used only in Lemma 7.3 and is removed in PAPER-LI-LIU-22 (Theorem 4.21). Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 (nonvanishing of the π-localized Chow group)
items.statement: Let (π, V_π) be as in Assumption 1.3 with |S_π| odd, and assume Hypothesis 6.6. If L′(1/2, π) ≠ 0 (ord_{s=1/2} L(s, π) = 1), then for every finite R ⊇ R_π with |R ∩ V^spl_F| ≥ 2: colim_{L_R} (CH^r(X_{L_R L^R})^0_{Q^ac})_{𝔪^R_π} ≠ 0, the colimit over open compact L_R ⊆ H(F_R). In fact the subgroup generated by special cycles is already nonzero after localization (Remark 1.6(4)); Q^ac may be replaced by any field of definition of π^∞ (Remark 1.6(5)).
items.locator: Theorem 1.5 and Remark 1.6, pp.5–6; proof §11, pp.52–53, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Proof: assuming vanishing, Hecke operators t_{T₂} with χ^R_π(t_{T₂}) = 1 kill the special cycles, so by Lemma 11.1 the doubling integral of E′ vanishes; Proposition 3.13 supplies test vectors with nonzero local zeta integrals at R. The local index at u above S_π rests on Proposition 9.1 (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Theorem 1.7 (arithmetic inner product formula)
items.statement: Let (π, V_π) be as in Assumption 1.3 with |S_π| odd; assume Hypothesis 6.6 and Hypothesis 4.5 in codimension r. (1) For ϕ_i = ⊗ϕ_{iv} ∈ V_π with lowest-weight archimedean components and ⟨ϕ^c_{1v}, ϕ_{2v}⟩ = 1 there, and φ^∞_i ∈ S(V^r ⊗ A^∞_F): ⟨Θ_{φ^∞_1}(ϕ_1), Θ_{φ^∞_2}(ϕ_2)⟩^♮_{X,E} = (L′(1/2, π)/b_{2r}(0))·C_r^{[F:Q]}·Π_{v finite} Z^♮_{π_v,V_v}(ϕ^c_{1v}, ϕ_{2v}, φ^∞_{1v} ⊗ (φ^∞_{2v})^c), with C_r = (−1)^r 2^{−2r} π^{r²} Γ(1)⋯Γ(r)/(Γ(r+1)⋯Γ(2r)) [Liu11a, Conj. 3.11]. (2) If L′(1/2, π) ≠ 0, then Hom_{H(A^∞_F)}(π̃^∞, colim_L CH^r(X_L)^0_C) ≠ 0 for π̃^∞ the theta lift of π^∞.
items.locator: Theorem 1.7 and Remark 1.8(1),(3), pp.6–7; proof §11, p.53, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: The height lies a priori in C ⊗ Q_ℓ; the identity shows it lies in C and is independent of ℓ (footnote 4). arXiv v5 prints C_r with 2^{r(r−1)} (sourceIssues E1); the item uses the final value. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Corollary 1.9 and Remark 1.10 (explicit height of new vectors)
items.statement: In Theorem 1.7(1) with R_π = ∅, ϕ_1 = ϕ_2 = ϕ in the one-dimensional space V^{[r]∅}_π of holomorphic new forms normalized everywhere, and φ^∞_v = 1_{(Λ^∅_v)^r}: ⟨Θ_{φ^∞}(ϕ), Θ_{φ^∞}(ϕ)⟩^♮_{X,E} = (−1)^r·(L′(1/2, π)/b_{2r}(0))·C_r^{[F:Q]}·Π_{v∈S_π} q_v^{r−1}(q_v + 1)/((q_v^{2r−1} + 1)(q_v^{2r} − 1)). Assuming injectivity of the étale Abel–Jacobi map and Beilinson's positivity conjecture, this is equivalent to L′(1/2, π) ≥ 0 (Remark 1.10).
items.locator: Corollary 1.9 and Remark 1.10, pp.7–8; proof p.53, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

items.statement: If |S_π| is even, so V_π ≃ V ⊗_F A_F for a hermitian space V over E, the classical theta lifts with Gaussian archimedean data satisfy ⟨θ_{φ^∞_1}(ϕ_1), θ_{φ^∞_2}(ϕ_2)⟩_H = (L(1/2, π)/b_{2r}(0))·C_r^{[F:Q]}·Π_{v finite} Z^♮_{π_v,V_v}(…) (Petersson product for the Tamagawa measure); in §11 it is applied (via [Liu11a, (2-6)] and Proposition 3.6(2)) to show that the doubling integral of the coherent Eisenstein series built from 1_{(Λ⋆_u)^{2r}} vanishes.

items.name: The doubling method: degenerate principal series, Siegel Eisenstein series and local doubling zeta integrals
items.statement: W^□_r = W_r ⊕ W̄_r identified with W_{2r}, G^□_r ⊇ G_r × G_r, P^□_r, δ^□_r, the element w_r with P^□_r w_r(G_r × G_r) open; I^□_{r,v}(s) = Ind(|·|^s_{E_v} ∘ δ^□_{r,v}), standard sections f^{(s)}, the Siegel–Weil section f_Φ(g) = ω^□_r(g)Φ(0), E(s, g, Φ) = Σ_{γ ∈ P^□_r(F)\G^□_r(F)} f^{(s)}_Φ(γg); the local doubling zeta integral Z(ϕ^∨ ⊗ ϕ, f^{(s)}) = ∫_{G_r(F_v)} ⟨π^∨(g)ϕ^∨, ϕ⟩ f^{(s)}(w_r(g, 1_{2r})) dg for good sections [Yam14, Def. 3.1], its normalization Z^♮ = (L(s + 1/2, π_v)/b_{2r,v}(s))^{−1} Z, and the functional Z^♮_{π_v,V_v} on π^∨_v ⊗ π_v ⊗ S(V^{2r}_v); absolute convergence at s = 0 and finiteness of L(s + 1/2, π_v)/b_{2r,v}(s) at s = 0 [Yam14, Lemma 7.2] (Remark 3.5).

items.name: Assumption 3.1 and Remark 3.2
items.statement: π an irreducible cuspidal subrepresentation with π_v the discrete series containing κ^r_{r,v} at archimedean v, unramified (resp. almost unramified) with respect to K_{r,v} at v ∉ R with ϵ_v = 1 (resp. −1), and tempered at all finite v; then V^{[r]R}_π ≠ 0. When R ⊆ V^spl_F, V is the hermitian space determined by π via local theta dichotomy.

items.name: Definition 3.3 and Remark 3.4 (the doubling L-function)
items.statement: L(s, π) = Π_v L(s, π_v) with the doubling L-factor of [Yam14, Thm. 5.2] at finite v and L(s, BC(π_v)) at archimedean v, where BC(π_v) is induced from arg^{n−1} ⊠ arg^{n−3} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ arg^{1−n}, so L(s + 1/2, π_v) = (Π_{i=1}^r 2(2π)^{−(s+i)}Γ(s + i))² (3.2). At split v and inert v ∉ R, L(s, π_v) = L(s, BC(π_v)) [Yam14, Thm. 7.2; Liu22, Rem. 1.4].
items.locator: Definition 3.3, (3.2) and Remark 3.4, p.15, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (local doubling multiplicity one and theta dichotomy)
items.statement: For π as in Assumption 3.1: (1) dim Hom_{G_r(F_v) × G_r(F_v)}(I^□_{r,v}(0), π_v ⊠ π^∨_v) = 1 for every finite v; (2) for v ∈ (V^fin_F \ R) ∪ V^spl_F, V_v is the unique hermitian space of rank 2r with Z^♮_{π_v,V_v} ≠ 0; (3) Θ(π_v, V_v) = Hom_{G_r(F_v)}(S(V^r_v), π_v) is irreducible, and nonzero for v ∈ (V^fin_F \ R) ∪ V^spl_F. Proof: seesaw identity, semisimplicity [GI16, Thm. 4.1(v)], Howe duality [GT16, Thm. 1.2], theta dichotomy [GG11, Thm. 1.8; HKS96], degenerate principal series [KS97, Thms. 1.2–1.3], and [Liu22, Prop. 5.6, Lemma 6.1].
items.locator: Proposition 3.6 and proof, pp.16–17, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

When V is coherent, d^♮h is the Tamagawa measure. (The local Whittaker function W_{T□}(s, g, Φ_v) of (3.3) is entire [Liu11a, Lemma 2.8(1)].)

items.name: Proposition 3.10, Definition 3.11 and Remark 3.12 (nonsingular Fourier expansions of incoherent Eisenstein series)
items.statement: For V incoherent: (1) if supp(^uΦ_v) ⊆ (^uV^{2r}_v)_reg for v in a nonempty R′ ⊆ R, then E(0, g, ^uΦ) = Σ_{T□ ∈ Herm°_{2r}(F)} Π_v W_{T□}(0, g_v, ^uΦ_v) on P^□_r(F_{R′})G^□_r(A^{R′}_F); (2) if supp(Φ_v) ⊆ (V^{2r}_v)_reg for v in R′ with |R′| ≥ 2, then E′(0, g, Φ) = Σ_{w ∉ V^spl} 𝔈(g, Φ)_w, 𝔈(g, Φ)_w = Σ_{Diff(T□,V) = {w}} W′_{T□}(0, g_w, Φ_w)Π_{v≠w} W_{T□}(0, g_v, Φ_v) [Liu11b, §2B]. E_{T_1,T_2} and 𝔈_{T_1,T_2} restrict the sums to ∂_{r,r}T□ = (T_1, T_2), and ∂_{r,r} maps Herm°_{2r}(F)^+ into Herm°_r(F)^+ × Herm°_r(F)^+.
items.locator: Proposition 3.10, Definition 3.11 and Remark 3.12, pp.18–19, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Proposition 3.13 (test functions with regular support)
items.statement: For π as in Assumption 3.1, a finite v with Z^♮_{π_v,V_v} ≠ 0, and nonzero ϕ_v ∈ π_v, ϕ^∨_v ∈ π^∨_v, there are φ_v, φ^∨_v ∈ S(V^r_v) with supp(φ_v ⊗ φ^∨_v) ⊆ (V^{2r}_v)_reg and Z^♮_{π_v,V_v}(ϕ^∨_v, ϕ_v, φ_v ⊗ φ^∨_v) ≠ 0. Proof: via the open cell ι : Ω → P_r w_r N_r, Z(ϕ^∨ ⊗ ϕ, f_Ψ) = ∫_Ω ξ^♭_{ϕ^∨,ϕ} Ψ̂ (3.6), temperedness gives ξ ∈ L^{2+ε} (modulo the centre when E = F × F), and Lemmas A.1–A.2 produce Ψ ∈ S(Herm°_{2r}(F)) with nonzero integral; the part pushed forward from the other hermitian space V′ contributes zero by Proposition 3.6.
items.locator: Proposition 3.13 and proof, (3.4)–(3.6), pp.19–21, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Lemma A.1 (Fourier support of L^{2+ε} functions)
items.statement: For F non-archimedean, X a finite-dimensional F-vector space, Δ a nonzero homogeneous polynomial on X and r ≥ 0: if f is a nonzero locally constant function on an open Ω ⊆ {Δ ≠ 0}, locally integrable on X, with ∫_Ω |f|^{2+ε}|Δ|^{rε}_F dx < ∞ for every ε > 0, then the support of f̂ (a distribution on X^∨) is not contained in an analytic hypersurface. Proof by Hausdorff–Young, Hölder and a tubular-neighbourhood volume estimate, as in [AN04, Thm. 1].
items.locator: Lemma A.1 and proof, pp.53–54, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: The exponents were rechecked: (A.1) gives q^{N(n−da)(δ+ε)/(2+ε)} with a = r(2−δ)ε/(δ+ε), and a choice δ < 2/n, ε → 0 makes the final exponent negative. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Lemma A.2 (the split variant)
items.statement: As Lemma A.1 for Ω = {Δ ≠ 0} and f on Ω, under a decomposition X = X_1 ⊕ X_2 ⊕ X_3 with dim X_1 = dim X_2 > 0 such that Ω is disjoint from X_1 ⊕ X_3 ∪ X_2 ⊕ X_3, |Δ| and |f| are invariant under α·(x_1, x_2, x_3) = (αx_1, α^{−1}x_2, x_3), and ∫_{F^×\Ω} |f|^{2+ε}|Δ|^{rε} < ∞ for every ε > 0: the support of f̂ is not contained in an analytic hypersurface.
items.locator: Lemma A.2 and proof, pp.55–57, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: The proof sums over the shells A^m_0 × A^m_i × B^{n−2m}_{−N} and then keeps the index i on the right-hand side (sourceIssues E7); the exponent condition in the final display was rechecked. items.name: Notation 3.14 (automorphic base change and archimedean characters)
items.statement: Π the automorphic base change of π to GL_n(A_E) (existence by [Shi], [KMSW]; uniqueness by strong multiplicity one), with Π_v induced from arg^{n−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ arg^{1−n} at archimedean v; I = {n − 1, n − 3, …, 1 − n}; characters χ : μ_2^I → C^× of signature (p, q) and the discrete series π^χ of U(p, q), π^χ_∞ on ^uH(F_∞) for signature (n − 1, 1); Π = Π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_s with conjugate-self-dual cuspidal Π_j and the induced partition I = I_1 ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ I_s.

items.name: Arthur's multiplicity formula and endoscopic classification for unitary groups
items.statement: The endoscopic classification of representations of quasi-split unitary groups and their inner forms [Mok15; KMSW]: the automorphic base change BC(π) is an isobaric sum of distinct cuspidal representations; Arthur's multiplicity formula for tempered global L-packets [KMSW, Thm. 1.7.1] (coherent characters χ = {χ_v} of A_Π give the discrete automorphic representations ⊗π^{χ_v} of U(V^χ) with multiplicity one; incoherent ones do not occur), and local–global compatibility at archimedean and split places; used in Notation 3.14, Lemma 3.15, Remark 3.16, Proposition 6.9 and Lemma 9.2.
items.locator: Notation 3.14, Lemma 3.15, Proposition 6.9 and Lemma 9.2(a)–(d), pp.21–22, 31, 41–42, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: ML.4 gives the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs (packets, multiplicities, local–global compatibilities) explicit owners.

items.name: Galois representations of conjugate-self-dual cuspidal representations and their purity
items.statement: For each Π_j, a semisimple ρ_{Π_j} : Gal(Q^ac/E) → GL_{n_j}(Q̄_ℓ) [Car12, Thm. 1.1], whose Weil–Deligne representations at finite places are pure (proof of [Car12, Thm. 7.4]), so H¹(E_u, ρ^c_{Π_j}(r)) = 0 [Nek07b, Prop. 4.2.2(1)].
items.locator: Notation 3.14(4), p.21; proof of Proposition 6.9, p.31, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: AG2.2 constructs the representations of polarized cuspidal systems; AG2.5 proves the ramified local–global comparison including the Caraiani upgrade.

items.name: Lemma 3.15 (which nearby-space representations contribute to middle cohomology)
items.statement: For π̃^∞ with Π_v the standard base change of π̃^∞_v for almost all v, exactly one holds: (a) no χ of signature (n − 1, 1) makes π^χ_∞ ⊗ π̃^∞ cuspidal automorphic on ^uH(A_F); (b) there is a unique j(π̃^∞) such that π^χ_∞ ⊗ π̃^∞ is cuspidal automorphic iff the μ_2-generator where χ = −1 lies in I_{j(π̃^∞)}. Moreover dim Hom_{H(A^∞_F)}(π̃^∞, colim_L H^{n−1}_dR(X_L/C)) is 0 in case (a) and n_{j(π̃^∞)} > 0 in case (b) (Matsushima's formula, [KMSW, Thm. 1.7.1], and one-dimensional middle (g, K)-cohomology of discrete series [BW00, II Thm. 5.4]).
items.locator: Lemma 3.15 and proof, pp.21–22, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Remark 3.16 (root numbers and the case (b))
items.statement: If π̃^∞ = Hom_{G_r(A^∞_F)}(S(V^r ⊗ A^∞_F), π^∞) ≠ 0 (irreducible by Proposition 3.6(3)), then ε(Π) = −1 [GI16, Thm. 4.1(ii)], and π̃^∞ is in case (b) of Lemma 3.15 iff exactly one j has ε(Π_j) = −1, in which case j = j(π̃^∞) (Arthur's multiplicity formula and Conjecture (P1)_n proved in [GI16, §4.4]); if ord_{s=1/2} L(s, Π) = 1 this holds automatically.
items.locator: Remark 3.16, p.22, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: The unitary Shimura varieties X_L
items.statement: For V incoherent with fixed u-nearby space ^uV (u the place induced by ι), the Shimura varieties X_L of Res_{F/Q} ^uH, smooth quasi-projective over E of dimension n − 1 (projective when F ≠ Q), with complex uniformization (X_L ⊗_E C)^an ≃ ^uH(F)\^u𝔇 × H(A^∞_F)/L (4.1), ^u𝔇 the negative lines in ^uV ⊗_E C, with the Deligne homomorphism of [LTXZZ, §3.2].
items.locator: §4, (4.1), p.22, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: V1 plans the analytic tower and V6 canonical models of abelian type, which covers these PEL-type unitary data.

items.name: Definition 4.1 and Remark 4.2 (Kudla's special cycles in Chow groups)
items.statement: For x ∈ V^m ⊗ A^∞_F (1 ≤ m ≤ n − 1): Z(x)_L = 0 if T(x) ∉ Herm_m(F)^+; if T(x) ∈ Herm°_m(F)^+, choose x′ ∈ ^uV^m and h with hx = x′, and let Z(x)_L ∈ Z^m(X_L) be the image cycle of X^{x′}_{hLh^{−1} ∩ H_{x′}(A^∞_F)} → X_{hLh^{−1}} →(·h) X_L, H_{x′} = U(V^⊥_{x′}); in general Z(x)_L ∈ CH^m(X_L)_Q [Liu11a, §3A]. For φ^∞ ∈ S(V^m ⊗ A^∞_F)^L and T ∈ Herm_m(F): Z_T(φ^∞)_L = Σ_{x ∈ L\V^m ⊗ A^∞_F, T(x) = T} φ^∞(x)Z(x)_L ∈ CH^m(X_L)_C, a cycle when T ∈ Herm°_m(F)^+.
items.locator: Definition 4.1 and Remark 4.2, pp.22–23, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Placed with the generating functions, as in PAPER-LI-LIU-22; the integral models of these cycles go to UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Kudla's generating function and Lemmas 4.3–4.4
items.statement: Z_{φ^∞}(g)_L = Σ_{T ∈ Herm_m(F)^+} ω_{m,∞}(g_∞)φ^0_∞(T)·Z_T(ω^∞_m(g^∞)φ^∞)_L, a formal sum in CH^m(X_L)_C. Lemma 4.3: ω_{m,∞}(n(b)m(a))φ^0_∞(T)·Z_T(ω_m(n(b)m(a))φ^∞)_L = φ^0_∞(^t a^c Ta)·Z_{^t a^c Ta}(φ^∞)_L for a ∈ GL_m(E), b ∈ Herm_m(F) (from [Liu11a, Thm. 3.5]). Lemma 4.4: t^*Z_T(φ^∞)_L = Z_T(tφ^∞)_L for t ∈ T^R_C.
items.locator: §4 and Lemmas 4.3–4.4, pp.23–24, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Hypothesis 4.5 and Remark 4.6 (modularity of generating functions), assumed
items.statement: For every L, φ^∞ ∈ S(V^m ⊗ A^∞_F)^L and linear l : CH^m(X_L)_C → C, g ↦ l(Z_{φ^∞}(g)_L) converges absolutely and lies in A[r](G_m(F)\G_m(A_F)). Known for m = 1 [Liu11a, Thm. 3.5]; for m ≥ 2 the generating function is formally modular [Liu11a, Thm. 3.5]; the symplectic analogue over Q is [BWR15] (conjectured in [Kud04]).
items.locator: Hypothesis 4.5 and Remark 4.6, p.24, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: A hypothesis of Theorem 1.7 and Corollary 1.9, not of Theorem 1.5. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Proposition 4.7 (finite-dimensionality of the span of special cycles)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 4.5 in codimension m: (1) Z_{φ^∞}(−)_L lies in A[r](G_m(F)\G_m(A_F)) ⊗_C CH^m(X_L)_C; (2) φ^∞ ↦ Z_{φ^∞}(−)_L is G_m(A^∞_F) × T^R_C-equivariant. Proof: by the q-expansions f^{(i)}(q) = Σ_T Z_T(φ^{∞(i)})_L q^T and dim M^{(i)} ≤ dim M[r]_m(Γ^{(i)}) < ∞ (4.2).
items.locator: Proposition 4.7 and proof, (4.2), pp.24–25, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

items.name: Definition 4.8 (arithmetic theta lifting)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 4.5 in codimension r, for ϕ ∈ V^{[r]}_π and φ^∞ ∈ S(V^r ⊗ A^∞_F)^L: Θ_{φ^∞}(ϕ)_L = ∫_{G_r(F)\G_r(A_F)} ϕ^c(g)Z_{φ^∞}(g)_L dg ∈ CH^r(X_L)_C (by Proposition 4.7), with image Θ_{φ^∞}(ϕ) in CH^r(X)_C = colim_L CH^r(X_L)_C; Θ(π, V) is the span of all Θ_{φ^∞}(ϕ).
items.locator: Definition 4.8, p.25, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Notation 5.1 and Lemma 5.2 (moduli interpretation of X′_L)
items.statement: T_0(R) = {a ∈ E ⊗ R : Nm_{E/F} a ∈ R^×}; for a CM type Φ ∋ ι, E′ generated by E and the reflex field of Φ, and a rank-one skew-hermitian space W, the PEL moduli Y of CM abelian varieties of type Φ and level L_0 is smooth projective of dimension 0 over E′ [Kot92]. X′_L := X_L ⊗_E Y represents sextuples (A_0, λ_0, η_0; A, λ, η) with (A_0, λ_0, η_0) ∈ Y(S), (A, λ) a unitary O_E-abelian scheme of signature nΦ − ι + ι^c [LTXZZ, Defs. 3.4.2–3.4.3], and η an L-orbit of hermitian isomorphisms V ⊗ A^∞_F → Hom^{λ_0,λ}_{E⊗A^∞}(H_1(A_{0s}, A^∞), H_1(A_s, A^∞)), up to O_F-linear quasi-isogenies compatible with the data [RSZ20, §3.2; LTXZZ, §4.1].
items.locator: Notation 5.1 and Lemma 5.2, p.26, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

items.name: Lemma 5.5 (changing the complex embedding)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^{(∞)}_E there is an isomorphism of systems {X_L ⊗_{E,ι_u} C} ≃ {^uX_L ⊗_{ι_u(E)} C} under which Z(x)_L ⊗_{E,ι_u} C corresponds to ^uZ(x)_L ⊗ C for x ∈ V^r ⊗ A^∞_F with T(x) ∈ Herm°_r(F)^+ (via the moduli interpretations for CM types containing both ι_u and ι, and Lemma 5.4).

items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Notation 5.6 (admissible CM types and the integral model of Y)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^fin_E \ V^ram_E above p, with C ≅ Q̄_p inducing u: Φ is admissible if Φ_v induces one place v^c of E above split v and is pulled back from the maximal unramified subfield at inert v; K is generated by E_u and the reflex field (unramified over E_u when V^{(p)}_F ∩ V^ram_F = ∅), with residue field k and K̆; for L_0 maximal at p, the model 𝒴 over O_K of triples (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0) (signature Φ, p-principal λ_0, L^p_0-level [LTXZZ, Def. 4.1.2]) is finite étale over O_K [How12, Prop. 3.1.2].
items.locator: Notation 5.6, p.28, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

items.name: Integral models 𝒳_m with Drinfeld level at a split place
items.statement: For u ∈ V^spl_E with V^{(p)}_F ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F: the moduli 𝒳_m over O_K of tuples (A_0, λ_0, η^p_0; A, λ, η^p, {η_v}, η_{u,m}) (signature nΦ − ι_w + ι^c_w, λ[v^∞] an isogeny with kernel of order q_v^{1−ϵ_v}, Lie(A[u^{c,∞}]) of rank 1 with O_E acting by ι^c_w, L_v-level structures at split v ≠ u, and a Drinfeld level-m structure η_{u,m} on A[u^{c,∞}][p^m_u]) is regular, flat (smooth for m = 0) and projective over O_K, with 𝒳_m ⊗ K ≃ X′_{L_{u,m}L^u} ⊗ K [RSZ20, Thm. 4.5]; S^{R ∪ V^{(p)}_F} acts by étale correspondences.

items.note: Regularity for m > 0 uses that K is unramified over E_u (footnote 13). Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.statement: For u ∈ V^int_E above odd p with u ∉ S and V^{(p)}_F ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F (after rescaling so that ψ_{F,v} is unramified and each Λ^R_v is self-dual or almost self-dual): a projective system {𝒳_{L̃}} of smooth projective schemes over O_K with 𝒳_{L̃} ⊗ K = X′_{L̃} ⊗ K and finite étale transition maps [LZ, §11.2], so S^R acts by étale correspondences.

items.statement: For the smooth models at inert u: 𝒳^∧_{L̃} ≃ [^uH(F)\𝒩 × H(A^{∞,u}_F)/L̃^u] ×_{Spf O_K} 𝒴^∧ (8.2), compatibly in L̃, with 𝒳^∧_{L̃} the completion of 𝒳_{L̃} ⊗ O_K̆ along its supersingular locus and 𝒩 the relative unitary Rapoport–Zink space over Spf O_K̆ [LZ, §§2.1, 13.1].

items.name: Strictly semistable models at an almost self-dual inert place and their reduction
items.statement: For u ∈ V^int_E above S with p odd and unramified in E and V^{(p)}_F ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F: a projective system {𝒳_{L̃}} of strictly semistable projective schemes over O_K [LZ, §11.3] (using that u is unramified over Q, footnote 18) with generic fibre X′_{L̃} ⊗ K; its special fibre is Y°_{L̃} ∪ Y•_{L̃}, where Y° is a P^{2r−1}-fibration over ^uH(F)\^uH(A^∞_F)/L̃^u L⋆_u × (𝒴 ⊗ F̄_p) (L⋆_u hyperspecial), Y• is proper smooth of dimension 2r − 1, and Y† = Y° ∩ Y• is a relative Fermat hypersurface in Y° [LTXZZ, §§5.1–5.5].

items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 5.3 and Lemma 5.4 (moduli description of special cycles)
items.statement: For x ∈ V^r ⊗ A^∞_F with T(x) ∈ Herm°_r(F)^+, Z′(x)_L classifies septuples (A_0, λ_0, η_0; A, λ, η; x̃) with x̃ ∈ Hom_{O_E}(A^r_0, A)_Q and x̃_* ∈ η(Lx); (1) Z′(x)_L → X′_L is finite and unramified; (2) its image cycle Z(x)′_L equals the restriction of Z(x)_L to X′_L, via Z′(x)_L ≅ X^{x′}_{hLh^{−1} ∩ H_{x′}(A^∞_F)} ⊗_E Y (5.1).

items.name: Integral special cycles, their K-theory classes and their uniformization
items.statement: For p-basic φ^∞ (Definition 6.5) and T ∈ Herm°_m(F)^+: the finite unramified morphism 𝒵_T(φ^∞)_L → 𝒳_L extending Z′_T(φ^∞)_L → X′_L [LZ, §13.3]; for φ^∞ = φ^∞_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ φ^∞_r of characteristic functions, ^K𝒵_T(φ^∞)_L ∈ K^Z_0(𝒳_L)_C the component supported on 𝒵_T(φ^∞)_L of O_{𝒵_{t_1}} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{𝒵_{t_r}}, in F^r K^Z_0(𝒳_L)_C [GS87, Prop. 5.5], hence an extension of Z_T(φ^∞)′_L; the uniformization 𝒵_T(φ^∞)^∧_L = Σ_{x ∈ ^uH(F)\^uV^m, T(x) = T} Σ_{h ∈ H_x(F)\H(A^{∞,u}_F)/L^u} φ^{∞,u}(h^{−1}x)·(𝒩(x), h)_L × 𝒴^∧ (8.3), with 𝒩(x) the Kudla–Rapoport cycle [KR11, Def. 3.2]; and ^K𝒩(x) = [𝒩(x_1)] ∪ ⋯ ∪ [𝒩(x_m)] in K^{𝒩(x)}_0(𝒩) [Zha21, App. B].

items.statement: For x ∈ ^uV^{2r} with T(x) = T□ on the almost self-dual Rapoport–Zink space: χ(π^∧_* ^K𝒩(x)) = (b_{2r,u}(0)/log q_u)·(((q_u^{2r} − 1)/(q_u + 1))·W′_{T□}(0, 1_{4r}, 1_{(Λ^R_u)^{2r}}) − (log q_u/(q_u + 1))·W_{T□}(0, 1_{4r}, 1_{(Λ⋆_u)^{2r}})) [LZ, Thm. 10.5.1, Rem. 10.5.4], with q_u the residue cardinality of F in the fractions and of E in log q_u.

items.name: Definition 6.8 (the Hecke character χ^R_π and the maximal ideal 𝔪^R_π)
items.statement: With H^R_{W_r} = ⊗_{v ∉ R} H^{ϵ_v}_{W_r,v} (spherical Hecke algebras at split v) and θ^R : H^R_{W_r} → T^R_C, the algebra H^R_{W_r} acts on V^{[r]R}_π by a character χ^R_{π,W_r} factoring through θ^R; since π is cohomological, there is a unique χ^R_π : T^R_{Q^ac} → Q^ac with χ^R_{π,W_r} = (χ^R_π ⊗ C) ∘ θ^R, and 𝔪^R_π = ker χ^R_π.

items.name: Proposition 6.9 (tempering Hecke operators exist)
items.statement: For every L_R: (1) (S^R_{Q^ac})^0_{L_R} \ 𝔪^R_π ≠ ∅; (2) under Hypothesis 6.6, (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R} \ 𝔪^R_π ≠ ∅. Proof: (1) by Matsushima's formula, [Ram, Thm. A] and temperedness [KMSW] only degree 2r − 1 survives localization; (2) by Hochschild–Serre and the Weil conjectures for almost all u, and at the remaining u by H¹(E_u, ρ^c_{Π_j}(r)) = 0 from purity.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 and Lemma 7.2 (local indices at split places vanish)
items.statement: For |R′| ≥ 2, u ∈ V^spl_E with π_u a tempered principal series and V^{(p)}_F ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F, there are s^u_1, s^u_2 ∈ S^R_{Q^ac} \ 𝔪^R_π with I_{T_1,T_2}(φ^∞_1, φ^∞_2, s^u_1 s_1, s^u_2 s_2, g_1, g_2)^ℓ_{L,u} = 0 for every admissible sextuple and all (T_1, T_2); s^u_i = 1 if u ∉ R. Lemma 7.2 (u ∉ R): the closures of Z(x_1)′_L, Z(x_2)′_L in the smooth model 𝒳_0 are disjoint, since a common point would make A quasi-isogenous to A^{2r}_0, impossible by [RSZ20, Lemma 8.7]; then Proposition B.10 applies. In general, an ℓ-tempered s from Lemma 7.3 and Corollary B.15(1) reduces to Proposition B.13 on 𝒳_m.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1, Lemma 7.2 and proofs, (7.1)–(7.2), pp.32–36, authors' final version (20 October 2021)

items.name: Lemma 8.3 (products of tempering operators are ℓ-tempered on the smooth model)
items.statement: If s is a product of two elements of (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R}, it gives an ℓ-tempered Q^ac-étale correspondence of 𝒳_L: via H^{2r}_{𝒳_L ⊗ k}(𝒳_L, Q_ℓ(r)) → H^{2r}(𝒳_L, Q_ℓ(r)) → H^{2r}(X′_L, Q_ℓ(r)) (8.1), absolute purity, Hochschild–Serre and the Weil conjectures, Poincaré duality and smooth proper base change, each factor kills one graded piece.

The proof computes the intersection on 𝒳_L by Proposition B.13 and Lemma 8.3, restricts to the supersingular locus, uses (8.3) and the local identity χ(π^∧_*{}^K𝒩(x)) = (b_{2r,u}(0)/log q_u)W′_{T□} (8.4)–(8.6), and matches the other places through Definition 3.8.

Proof: by Corollary B.15 and Proposition 6.9(2) it suffices that H^i(Y°_L)_𝔪 = 0 and H^i(Y•_L)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≤ 2r − 2 and H^i(Y†_L)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≤ 2r − 3; the first because Π_u is ramified (so the hyperspecial invariants of the relevant packet members vanish, via Arthur's multiplicity formula, [Ram, Thm. A] and [LTXZZ, Lemma C.2.3]), the third by the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem and Poincaré duality, and the second from the weight spectral sequence, [LTXZZ, Prop. 5.5.4] and the nontrivial monodromy of ρ^c_{Π_1} at u forced by Hypothesis 6.6 (9.1).

items.name: Proposition 9.1 (local indices at inert places, almost self-dual level)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^int_E above S with p odd, unramified in E, and V^{(p)}_F ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F, and a fixed self-dual lattice Λ⋆_u of ^uV_u, there are s^u_1, s^u_2 ∈ S^R_{Q^ac} \ 𝔪^R_π with log q_u·vol^♮(L)·I_{T_1,T_2}(φ^∞_1, φ^∞_2, s^u_1 s_1, s^u_2 s_2, g_1, g_2)^ℓ_{L,u} = 𝔈_{T_1,T_2}((g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (s^u_1 s_1φ^∞_1 ⊗ (s^u_2 s_2φ^∞_2)^c))_u − (log q_u/(q_u^r − 1))·E_{T_1,T_2}((g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (s^u_1 s_1φ^{∞,u}_1 ⊗ (s^u_2 s_2φ^{∞,u}_2)^c) ⊗ 1_{(Λ⋆_u)^{2r}}). Proof as for Proposition 8.1 on the strictly semistable model, with vol(L_u) = (q + 1)(q^{2r} − 1)^{−1} and the almost self-dual intersection formula of [LZ, Thm. 10.5.1, Rem. 10.5.4] ((9.2)–(9.3)).

items.name: Green currents and the archimedean local index (10.2)
items.statement: For X smooth projective over C of dimension n − 1 and Z ∈ Z^r(X)_C, a Green current g_Z is an (r − 1, r − 1)-current, smooth off supp Z, with dd^c g_Z + δ_Z = [ω_Z] for a smooth tail form ω_Z; for Z homologically trivial it is harmonic (g^♥_Z) if ω_Z = 0; for disjointly supported homologically trivial Z_1, Z_2, ⟨Z_1, Z_2⟩_{X,C} = ½ ∫_{X(C)} g^♥_{Z_1} ∧ δ_{Z^c_2}, independent of the harmonic Green current.
items.locator: §10, (10.2), p.45, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Kudla–Millson Green currents and the archimedean comparison of Liu
items.statement: For the cycles s^*_i Z_{T_i}(ω^∞_r(g^∞_i)φ^∞_i)_L on X_L ⊗_E C there are Kudla–Millson Green currents g^KM_{T_i}(φ^∞_i, s_i, g_i)_L with tail forms ω^KM_{T_i} (proof of [Liu11a, Thm. 4.20]); with I^KM (10.4) the modified index, vol^♮(L)·I^KM_{T_1,T_2}(…)_{L,u} = ½ 𝔈_{T_1,T_2}((g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (s_1φ^∞_1 ⊗ (s_2φ^∞_2)^c))_u (10.5) [Liu11a, Thm. 4.20], with the sign Π_v γ^{2n}_{V_v} = 1 in place of Π_v γ_{V_v} = −1 (footnote 20; reproved in [GS19, Cor. 5.12]). The integral of ϕ^c against the Kudla–Millson form of the generating function is a harmonic (r, r)-form [Mil85, Thm. III.2.1; KM86, §3] (10.9).
items.locator: §10, (10.4)–(10.5), (10.9) and footnote 20, pp.45–49, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Footnote 20 corrects a sign in [Liu11a, Thm. 4.20]; that correction is the paper's, not a mistake in it. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Proposition 10.1 and Remark 10.2 (local indices at archimedean places, after averaging)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^{(∞)}_E, an admissible sextuple, ϕ_1 ∈ V^{[r]R}_π, K_1 fixing φ^∞_1 and ϕ_1, a Siegel fundamental domain 𝔉_1 for G_r(F) ∩ g^∞_1 K_1(g^∞_1)^{−1} and T_2 ∈ Herm°_r(F)^+: vol^♮(L)·∫_{𝔉_1} ϕ^c(τ_1g_1) Σ_{T_1} I_{T_1,T_2}(φ^∞_1, φ^∞_2, s_1, s_2, τ_1g_1, g_2)_{L,u} dτ_1 = ½ ∫_{𝔉_1} ϕ^c(τ_1g_1) Σ_{T_1} 𝔈_{T_1,T_2}((τ_1g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (s_1φ^∞_1 ⊗ (s_2φ^∞_2)^c))_u dτ_1 (10.1), both sides absolutely convergent. No termwise comparison (holomorphic projection) is needed: the difference is the pairing of a harmonic, cohomologically trivial, hence zero, (r, r)-form (10.9) with η + g^KM_{T_2}, where η := −g^♥_{T_2}(φ^∞_2, s_2, g^∞_2)^c_L.

items.name: Lemma 11.1 (assembling the local indices)
items.statement: In the setting of §11 (S = S_π, R ⊆ V^spl_F with R_π ⊆ R, |R| ≥ 2, R′ = R, s_i with χ^R_π(s_i) = 1, s̃_i = s_i Π_u s^u_i): (1) for T_2 ∈ Herm°_r(F)^+, t ∈ T^R_{Q^ac} and g_2 ∈ G_r(A^R_F), vol^♮(L)·Σ_j ∫_{𝔉^{(j)}} ϕ^c_1(τg^{(j)}) Σ_{T_1} I_{T_1,T_2}(tφ^∞_1, φ^∞_2, s̃_1, s̃_2, τg^{(j)}, g_2)^ℓ_L dτ = χ^R_π(t)^c ∫ ϕ^c_1(g_1)E′(0, (g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ Φ^∞)_{−,T_2} dg_1 − χ^R_π(t)^c Σ_{u ∈ S_E} (log q_u/(q_u^r − 1)) ∫ ϕ^c_1(g_1)E(0, (g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ Φ^{∞,u} ⊗ 1_{(Λ⋆_u)^{2r}})_{−,T_2} dg_1; (2) the double integral over both variables of the global indices equals (L′(1/2, π)/b_{2r}(0))·C_r^{[F:Q]}·Π_v Z^♮_{π_v,V_v}(ϕ^c_{1v}, ϕ_{2v}, φ^∞_{1v} ⊗ (φ^∞_{2v})^c), the coherent terms vanishing by the Rallis inner product formula and Proposition 3.6(2).

items.name: Beilinson's non-archimedean local index (B.1), Definition B.2, Remark B.1 and Lemma B.3
items.statement: For X smooth projective of pure dimension n − 1 over a non-archimedean local field K and ℓ invertible on k: Z^d(X)^{⟨ℓ⟩} = ker cl_{X,ℓ}; Z^{d_1,d_2}(X) and Z^{d_1,d_2}(X)^{⟨ℓ⟩} (d_1 + d_2 = n) spanned by pairs supported on disjoint closed Z_1, Z_2; ⟨c_1, c_2⟩^ℓ_{X,K} ∈ C ⊗ Q_ℓ is the image of γ_1 ∪ γ_2 under H^{2n−2}(U_1 ∩ U_2, Q_ℓ(n)) → H^{2n−1}(X, Q_ℓ(n)) → H¹(K, Q_ℓ(1)) = Q_ℓ, where γ_i ∈ H^{2d_i−1}(U_i, Q_ℓ(d_i)) lifts the refined cycle class cl^{Z_i}_{X,ℓ}(c_i) [Beĭ87, §2]; it is conjugate symmetric, independent of choices, invariant under finite base extension and multiplied by deg u under finite étale u (Lemma B.3). Remark B.1: under the monodromy–weight conjecture Z^d(X)^{⟨ℓ⟩} is independent of ℓ.
items.locator: Remark B.1, Definition B.2, (B.1) and Lemma B.3, pp.57–58, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Lemma B.4 and Remark B.5 (the local index via a projective model)
items.statement: For π : 𝒳 → Spec O_K projective with generic fibre X and special fibre Y, c_i supported on disjoint Z_i: for β_1 ∈ H^{2d_1}_{Y ∪ Z_1}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(d_1)) lifting cl^{Z_1}(c_1) with zero image in H^{2d_1}(𝒳), and β_2 ∈ H^{2d_2−2(n−1)}_{Y ∪ Z_2}(𝒳, π^!Q_ℓ(d_2 − n + 1)) lifting cl^{Z_2}(c_2), the trace of β_1 ∪ β_2 ∈ H²_Y(𝒳, π^!Q_ℓ(1)) is ⟨c_1, c_2⟩^ℓ_{X,K} ([Beĭ87, Lemma-def. 2.1.1], stated there without proof); for 𝒳 regular, π^!Q_ℓ[2 − 2n](1 − n) ≅ Q_ℓ by absolute purity (Remark B.5).
items.locator: Lemma B.4, proof and Remark B.5, pp.58–60, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Lemma B.6 (Chern classes of cycle classes are refined cycle classes)
items.statement: For c ∈ Z^d_Z(X), cl^Z_{X,ℓ}([c]) ∈ H^{2d}_Z(X, Q_ℓ(d)) (Gillet's Chern class of the K-theory class) equals the refined cycle class cl^Z_{X,ℓ}(c): reduce to Z smooth by semi-purity [Fuj02, §8], then [Gil81, Thm. 3.1].
items.locator: Lemma B.6 and proof, p.61, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Definition B.7 and Lemma B.8 (the intersection pairing on K-groups with supports)
items.statement: For 𝒳 regular and closed Z_1, Z_2 ⊆ 𝒳 with Z_1 ∩ Z_2 ⊆ Y: C_1.C_2 = χ(π_*(C_1 ∪ C_2)) on K^{Z_1}_0(𝒳)_C × K^{Z_2}_0(𝒳)_C (linear, conjugate linear). Lemma B.8: for C_i ∈ F^{d_i}K^{Z_i}_0(𝒳), C_1.C_2 is the image of cl^{Z_1}_{𝒳,ℓ}(C_1) ∪ cl^{Z_2}_{𝒳,ℓ}(C_2) under H^{2n}_{Z_1∩Z_2}(𝒳) → H^{2n}_Y(𝒳) → H²_{Spec k}(Spec O_K, Q_ℓ(1)) = Q_ℓ (by [GS87, Prop. 5.5] and the proof of [Gil81, Prop. 2.35], footnote 22).
items.locator: Definition B.7, Lemma B.8 and proof, pp.61–62, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: arXiv v5 cites [Gil81, Prop. 2.35] without the footnote-22 remark that it covers only Z_1 = Z_2 (sourceIssues E9). Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Definition B.9, Proposition B.10 and Remark B.11 (computing local indices by extensions)
items.statement: C ∈ F^d K^{Y ∪ supp(c)}_0(𝒳)_C is an extension of c ∈ Z^d(X)_C if C|_X = [c], and ℓ-flat if its class in H^{2d}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(d)) ⊗ C vanishes. Proposition B.10: for (c_1, c_2) ∈ Z^{d_1,d_2}(X)^{⟨ℓ⟩} with disjoint supports and extensions C_i ∈ F^{d_i}K^{Z_i}_0(𝒳)_C (Z_1 ∩ Z_2 ⊆ Y), one of them ℓ-flat: ⟨c_1, c_2⟩^ℓ_{X,K} = C_1.C_2; for π smooth, Zariski closures give ℓ-flat extensions and the index is in C and independent of ℓ (Remark B.11, which also defines it at u | ℓ).
items.locator: Definition B.9, Proposition B.10 and Remark B.11, p.62, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Proposition B.10 prints supp(c_i) ∩ supp(c_2) (sourceIssues E6). Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Definition B.12 and Proposition B.13 (ℓ-tempered correspondences)
items.statement: For n = 2r and d_1 = d_2 = r, an L-étale correspondence t of 𝒳 is ℓ-tempered if t^* annihilates H^{2r}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ L. Proposition B.13: then for c_1, c_2 ∈ Z^r(X)_C with supp(t^*c_1) ∩ supp(t^*c_2) = ∅, (t^*c_1, t^*c_2) ∈ Z^{r,r}(X)^{⟨ℓ⟩} and ⟨t^*c_1, t^*c_2⟩^ℓ_{X,K} = t^*C_1.t^*C_2 for arbitrary extensions C_i, so the index lies in C.
items.locator: Definition B.12 and Proposition B.13, p.63, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: Proposition B.14 and Corollary B.15 (a criterion for tempering)
items.statement: If Y_0 = Y^red ⊃ Y_1 ⊃ ⋯ is a finite stratification with Y°_j = Y_j \ Y_{j+1} regular of pure codimension n_j ≥ 1 in 𝒳, stabilized by t, and t^* kills H^{2r}(X, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ L and H^i(Y°_j ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ) ⊗ L for i ≤ 2r − 2n_j, then some power of t is ℓ-tempered (decreasing induction on j via absolute purity and Hochschild–Serre, m_j = m_{j+1} + 2). Corollary B.15: for a ring S of étale correspondences and a maximal ideal 𝔪 of S_L, (1) if (H^{2r}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ L)_𝔪 = 0 there is an ℓ-tempered element of S_L \ 𝔪; (2) if (H^{2r}(X, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ L)_𝔪 = 0 and (H^i(Y°_j ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ) ⊗ L)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≤ 2r − 2n_j and every j, for an S-stable stratification, then (H^{2r}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ L)_𝔪 = 0.
items.locator: Proposition B.14, Corollary B.15 and proofs, pp.63–64, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Corollary B.15 prints H^{2d}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(d)) for H^{2r}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(r)) (sourceIssues E6); the induction in Proposition B.14 was rechecked. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-LIU-22.

items.name: ℓ-adic and de Rham cycle class maps, with supports
items.statement: cl_{X,ℓ} : Z^d(X) → H^{2d}(X, Q_ℓ(d)) and the refined class cl^Z_{X,ℓ}(c) ∈ H^{2d}_Z(X, Q_ℓ(d)) for smooth X over a field of characteristic zero, and cl_dR.
items.locator: Notation 2.5, p.13; Appendix B, pp.57–58, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: EDC.3 constructs fundamental classes with support and the cycle class map for smooth varieties over perfect fields.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences over local and finite fields
items.statement: For varieties over E_u, K or k, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence relating cohomology over the field to Galois cohomology of geometric cohomology; used with weights for injectivity of H^{2r}(X_u, Q_ℓ(r)) → H^{2r}(X_u ⊗ Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r)) and in Proposition B.14.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 6.9, B.14 and Lemma 8.3, pp.31, 37, 64, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: R02.2 is the Hochschild–Serre owner.

items.name: The Weil conjectures (weights) for proper smooth varieties over finite fields
items.statement: Purity of the cohomology of proper smooth varieties over finite fields (and weight arguments for smooth varieties), used for injectivity of restriction to the geometric fibre and in the weight spectral sequence argument.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 6.9, Lemma 8.3 and Lemma 9.2, pp.31, 37, 43, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: R34.5 plans Weil I and the required Weil II results.

items.name: The weight spectral sequence of a strictly semistable scheme
items.statement: For a proper strictly semistable scheme over O_K, the weight spectral sequence E^{p,q}_1 ⇒ H^{p+q}(𝒳 ⊗ Q̄_p, Q_ℓ) built from the cohomology of the strata Y°, Y•, Y†, with the monodromy operator; used after localization at 𝔪 in Lemma 9.2.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 9.2, pp.42–43, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: LPV.7 constructs the weight spectral sequence for strict normal-crossing models "actually used by the analytic/Shimura consumer".

items.name: Gillet–Soulé K-groups with supports and their codimension filtration
items.statement: For Z ⊆ 𝒳 closed, K^Z_0(𝒳) of complexes with support in Z [GS87, §1.1] with the codimension filtration F^d, pushforward to K_0(Spec k), maps K^{Z′}_0 → K^Z_0 for Z′ ⊆ Z, cup products K^{Z_1}_0 × K^{Z_2}_0 → K^{Z_1∩Z_2}_0 with F^a ∪ F^b ⊆ F^{a+b} rationally [GS87, Prop. 5.5], the map [ ] : ⊕_{d′≥d} Z^{d′}_Z(𝒳) → F^d K^Z_0(𝒳) (B.3), and agreement with Quillen K-theory with supports for regular 𝒳.
items.locator: Appendix B, (B.3), pp.60–61, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: S.6 plans products with supports and Adams operations; S.7 Chern classes and the comparison with Chow groups in the regular setting.

items.name: Gillet's ℓ-adic Chern classes with supports
items.statement: cl^Z_{𝒳,ℓ} : F^d K^Z_0(𝒳) → H^{2d}_Z(𝒳, Q_ℓ(d)) for regular 𝒳 [Gil81, Def. 2.34(ii)] with S = Spec O_K and ℓ-adic cohomology, compatible with cup products [Gil81, Prop. 2.35] and with refined cycle classes on smooth varieties [Gil81, Thm. 3.1].
items.locator: Appendix B, pp.61–62, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: M.8 constructs étale Chern classes with product compatibilities.

items.name: Igusa varieties of the first kind and Mantovan's Igusa varieties
items.statement: I_{m,j} with Y°_{m,j} a finite disjoint union of copies [HT01, §IV.1], forming projective systems with finite étale transitions; Mantovan's I^j_{Mant,m} (finite Galois covers of I_{m,j}) and the perfection Ig_j of lim_m I^j_{Mant,m} [CS17, Prop. 4.3.8].
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.3 and footnote 15, pp.35–36, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: IG.1 constructs Igusa towers, their finite-level models and perfected limits.

items.name: Caraiani–Scholze: generic concentration and the Igusa trace formula
items.statement: [CS17, Cor. 6.1.4]: localized at a generic 𝔪, H^i(Ig_b ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ)_𝔪 vanishes outside the middle degree d_b; [CS17, Thm. 5.5.7] (with the modification in the proof of [LTXZZ, Thm. D.1.3]): the alternating cohomology [H_c(I^j_Mant ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ)] as a Hecke module in terms of automorphic representations; used, with [Ram, Thm. A], to force j = 0 in Lemma 7.3. The source assumes hyperspecial level at p; footnote 16 asserts the argument works with only L_u hyperspecial.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.3 and footnote 16, pp.35–36, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: IG.4 plans the semiperversity and support bounds, IG.5 the rational Igusa trace comparison.

items.name: Absolute purity (Gabber; Fujiwara)
items.statement: For a regular closed immersion Z → 𝒳 of pure codimension c of regular schemes with ℓ invertible, H^i_Z(𝒳, Q_ℓ(j)) ≅ H^{i−2c}(Z, Q_ℓ(j − c)) [Fuj02]; used in Lemma 8.3, Lemma 9.2, Remark B.5 and Proposition B.14, and semi-purity [Fuj02, §8] in Lemma B.6.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 8.3, 9.2, B.6, Remark B.5 and Proposition B.14, pp.37, 42, 60–61, 64, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2 explicitly excludes Gabber's absolute purity. Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 as a source, where PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 routes its absolute-purity input.

items.name: Newton strata of the special fibre of 𝒳_m
items.statement: Y_m = 𝒳_m ⊗ k, Y_{m,0} = Y^red_m, and Y_{m,j} (0 ≤ j ≤ n − 1) the closed locus where the formal part of A[u^{c,∞}] has height at least j + 1; Y°_{m,j} = Y_{m,j} \ Y_{m,j+1} is smooth over k of pure dimension n − 1 − j (as [HT01, Cor. III.4.4]; parallel to X^{(n−1−j)}_{U^p,m} of [HT01, §III.4], footnote 14).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.3 and footnote 14, pp.34–35, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 7.3 and Remark 7.4 (vanishing of localized middle cohomology of 𝒳_m)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 7.1 with p ≠ ℓ (π_u a tempered principal series), for every m ≥ 0: (H^{2r}(𝒳_m, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ Q^ac)_𝔪 = 0 with 𝔪 = 𝔪^R_π ∩ S^{R ∪ V^{(p)}_F}_{Q^ac}. Proof: by Corollary B.15(2) and Proposition 6.9(2) it suffices that H^i(Y°_{m,j} ⊗ F̄_p)_𝔪 = 0 unless j = 0 and i = 2r − 1; for the maximal j with nonzero cohomology, [CS17, Cor. 6.1.4] gives concentration in degree 2r − 1 − j, and [CS17, Thm. 5.5.7] with Π_u ≃ π_u tempered principal series and [Ram, Thm. A] force j = 0. Remark 7.4 conjectures the lemma without the principal-series condition (proved in PAPER-LI-LIU-22, Theorem 4.21).
items.locator: Lemma 7.3, proof and Remark 7.4, pp.34–35, authors' final version (20 October 2021)
items.note: The proof writes d = n − j = 2r − 1 − j (sourceIssues E4). Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.
